question.text: When an investor redeems units from an open-ended mutual fund scheme, the immediate impact on the scheme's NAV is:

answer.text: NAV decreases because assets are reduced
NAV increases because fewer units remain
No change in NAV because both assets and units decrease proportionally
NAV becomes zero if all units are redeemed

explanation.text: The Logic: A redemption is processed at NAV, so both net assets and units outstanding fall by the same proportion. Because NAV equals net assets divided by units, the per-unit value is unchanged by a redemption or by an additional investment. The Trap: It can feel as if losing assets must reduce NAV, but the simultaneous fall in units outstanding preserves the per-unit value. Note: Redemption and fresh subscriptions do not directly move the NAV; the NAV reflects the underlying portfolio's valuation per unit.
